basics.name: Anmoldeep Singh
basics.summary: Master's student in Computational Science and Engineering at the Technical University of Munich with a background in Mechanical Engineering and industrial experience in computational modeling, renewable energy, and engineering innovation. Interested in scientific computing, computational fluid dynamics, numerical methods, machine learning, and high-performance computing, with a particular interest in combining physics-based and data-driven methods for scientific and engineering applications.

work.name: Technical University of Munich
work.summary: Research work involving computational materials science, automated simulation workflows, and data-driven analysis.
highlights: Developing automated high-throughput simulation workflows for Ni-based alloy design using Python and CALPHAD models.
Analyzing phase diagrams, microstructure evolution, and composition–property relationships using large-scale simulation data.
Optimizing computational workflows to support advanced alloy development.

work.name: Thermax Limited
work.summary: Worked on computational modeling, renewable energy, sustainable combustion, process optimization, and engineering innovation projects.
highlights: Developed a Python-based hybrid mathematical model for smart boiler control by integrating physics-based boiler dynamics with data-driven combustion and heat-transfer models.
Implemented Stochastic Gradient Descent with the ADAM optimizer to continuously improve model parameters under changing operating conditions.
Achieved approximately 95% agreement with field data during model validation.

Developed and validated a Vapor Pressure Swing Adsorption and membrane hybrid solution for biomethane purification, reducing methane slippage by approximately 50% compared with conventional double-VPSA systems.
Worked on mathematical modeling of high-strength H2S removal using coupled scrubber and bioreactor models for biomethane purification.
Conducted Temperature Swing Adsorption benchmarking studies for green hydrogen dehydration and generated in-house adsorption–desorption and dew-point data.
Worked on mathematical modeling of heat exchangers and furnaces using stirred-reactor and plug-flow models, numerical methods, and physics-based and data-driven approaches.
Gained industrial experience in heat exchanger manufacturing, quality assurance, commissioning, troubleshooting, failure analysis, and root-cause analysis.

education.thesis: Artificial Neural Network for Modeling CH4-H2 Turbulent Combustion

projects.name: Aerodynamic Shape Optimization using CFD and Genetic Algorithms
projects.description: Automated aerodynamic optimization framework coupling an in-house CFD solver with a Genetic Algorithm to optimize geometries for reduced drag.
highlights: Developed an automated optimization pipeline coupling geometry generation, CFD simulation, fitness evaluation, and evolutionary search.
Implemented parameterized geometry generation and automated simulation workflows.
Used aerodynamic drag as the optimization objective to evolve improved geometries.

projects.name: Turbulent Combustion Modeling using Deep Learning
projects.description: Deep-learning surrogate model for CH4-H2 turbulent combustion integrated with OpenFOAM.
highlights: Conducted numerical investigation of turbulent reacting flows using OpenFOAM coupled with the Flamelet Progress Variable model.
Designed and trained a neural-network surrogate to replace the OpenFOAM FPV model.
Integrated the neural-network model into the CFD workflow for turbulent combustion simulations.
Achieved approximately 99% reduction in memory requirements compared with the original FPV-based representation.

projects.name: Deep Learning Framework in C++
projects.description: PyTorch-inspired deep learning framework implemented from scratch in modern C++ using standard libraries.
highlights: Implemented a Tensor abstraction supporting scalar, one-dimensional, and two-dimensional data.
Implemented tensor operations including element-wise operations and matrix multiplication.
Developed automatic differentiation functionality using computational graph relationships.
Built the project using CMake and tested core functionality using GoogleTest.
Developing the framework toward MNIST and Fashion-MNIST classification.

projects.name: Neural Network from Scratch in Python
projects.description: Implementation of a neural network from scratch using Python and fundamental numerical operations.
highlights: Implemented the forward and backward passes of a neural network without using a deep-learning framework.
Implemented core components including activation functions, softmax, loss calculation, and gradient-based optimization.
Trained and evaluated the network on the MNIST dataset.

projects.name: Smart Boiler Control
projects.description: Hybrid mathematical and data-driven modeling framework for boiler pressure and water-level control.
highlights: Developed a hybrid model combining physics-based boiler dynamics with data-driven combustion and heat-transfer models.
Implemented SGD with ADAM optimization for model parameter adaptation.
Achieved approximately 95% agreement with field data during validation.
Developed the Python codebase for automated control and reduced operational intervention.

projects.name: MiniCEA
projects.description: Thermochemical calculator for computing adiabatic flame temperature and heat of reaction for different fuel families.
highlights: Developed a Python program to calculate adiabatic flame temperature and heat of reaction for alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, and alcohols.
Implemented calculations based on specified fuel-to-air ratios.
Used OpenPyXL for data processing and PyPlot for graphical visualization.

projects.name: FMAE-FKDC 2021 Go-Kart Design Challenge
projects.description: Go-Kart design and simulation project conducted as part of the IIT Goa Motorsport Club.
highlights: Designed and validated Go-Kart chassis configurations according to competition constraints and safety requirements.
Performed impact simulations using Ansys Workbench to optimize structural safety and performance.
Led the mechanical team responsible for chassis design and simulation.
Secured 1st position in the EV category at the FMAE-FKDC National Online Go-Kart Design Competition.

Supported first-year undergraduate students through academic discussions and interactive learning activities.

Coordinated mechanical teams to ensure integration of vehicle components and systems.
Contributed to chassis design, structural analysis, and performance optimization.
